A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heuristic-based parallel-data curation study. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the documented changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original NMT experiments, heuristic ablations and human corpus-quality evaluations, including Tables 5, 6 and 8.

after.justification: V2 retains original NMT experiments and reports a revised human evaluation plus additional threshold and training-size experiments, including Tables 2, 6 and 11 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: V2 extends the noise-diagnosis component with the CCN overlapping-content category and revised annotation rules for short, untranslated and wrong-language content (Section 3; Tables 3 and 9). The filtering pipeline, including n-gram deduplication, embedding models and NMT architecture, remains substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 newly reports using a human-crafted En-Si-Ta validation dataset from Fernando et al. (2020) to calibrate STRatio thresholds. The main CCMatrix, CCAligned and FLORES+ coverage, three language pairs and translation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Both versions compare LASER3, XLM-R and LaBSE ranking and retain unfiltered top-ranked baselines against heuristic filtering. Additional discussion of other PDC systems does not introduce experimentally evaluated external comparators.

E3.justification: Human evaluation changes from sampling 100 pairs from the top 100,000 with three annotators per pair to sampling from the top 1,000 with two, using revised error categories. V2 adds training-size and sentence-cutoff protocols and replaces v1's inconsistent STRatio specification with language-specific calibrated ranges. These are documented protocol changes; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained heuristic ablations, v2 adds tests of 3/4/5-word cutoffs (Table 11), training sizes from 50k to 200k where available (Figure 5), explicit disparity analysis (Table 7), and per-filter corpus retention (Table 15). These substantially expand evidence about threshold selection, data quantity and filtering failures.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports Pearson inter-annotator agreement: 0.88 for En-Si, 0.68 for En-Ta and 0.49 for Si-Ta (Section 3). V1 reports averaged annotations without agreement statistics. Neither version supplies NMT repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or seed information.

E6.justification: The human-audit results are replaced under changed sampling and labeling conditions, and threshold, training-size and retention results are added. Most existing NMT scores remain unchanged, but some summaries change incorrectly: CCAligned En-Ta XLM-R's combined gain changes from +24.34 in v1 Table 5 to +12.30 in v2 Table 14, although both retain scores of 17.40 and 41.74.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive theoretical results or proofs, and v2 adds no formal derivations. Its taxonomy revisions and disparity calculations concern empirical classification and evaluation rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central claims that heuristics improve NMT and reduce disparities across embedding models are retained. V2 adds the extended noise taxonomy as an explicit contribution and reframes the contribution list away from v1's claim of the first comparative human evaluation.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving aggressive 4-gram filtering, LASER3's OPUS training, corpus depletion and LID weaknesses for Sinhala/Tamil. It qualifies the benefits of increasing training data and discusses persistent CCMatrix-XLM-R disparities. Limitations expand beyond language coverage to annotation staffing and LID quality.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands annotation documentation with qualifications, experience, a 30-pair training exercise, reported 1,200-pair assignments and a decision flowchart. It also documents OPUS acquisition, threshold calibration and filtered-corpus sizes. NMT hardware and hyperparameters are retained. Code/data release is announced, but footnote 1 defers it until acceptance.

R1.justification: The principal PDC literature and research focus remain. V2 adds supporting references such as Aulamo et al. (2020), Hangya and Fraser (2018), and Fernando et al. (2020), removes references including Van Noord et al. (2025), and refines positioning around taxonomy extension, systematic heuristic combinations and simplicity relative to model-based pipelines.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and results discussion are extensively rewritten. The heuristic review moves into related work, human evaluation moves into methodology, a standalone Discussion is added, and appendices are reorganized. Authorship and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: V1's appendix ablation table becomes v2's main Table 6 with revised formatting and highlighting; human-evaluation and summary tables are relocated and expanded. Several original bar plots are replaced by n-gram trend displays. New taxonomy, annotation-flowchart, disparity, threshold, training-size and corpus-retention displays substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful sensitivity evidence and substantially fuller annotation guidance, but introduces misleading summaries of central results. Section 5.3 reports post-filter overall errors of 2.17%, 2.50% and 1.00%; these are short-sentence-category averages, whereas Table 2's overall-error columns average 17.33%, 46.00% and 26.17%. Table 14 also misstates retained NMT gains. These reliability problems coexist with meaningful additions, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
